`satisfies` is implemented in `/tmp/agentdiff-haiku-zsnsndj7/work/ranges.py`. All 14 rule tests pass.

I went through each rule and edge case in the docstring and wrote a test for each. Two of my first-run failures were wrong expectations in my tests, not bugs in the code. The pre-release gate is keyed on the same MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, so `1.9.0-beta` can't satisfy `^1.2.3-beta`. I corrected those two tests. The test file is in the scratchpad (`test_ranges.py`), not in the project.

Choices the docstring didn't settle:
- **Caret/tilde partials:** `^1`, `^1.2`, `~1`, and `~1.2` are accepted, following npm. `^` and `~` reject wildcards, so `^1.x` is malformed.
- **Pre-release gate applies to `*`:** `1.2.3-rc` does not satisfy `*`, `x`, or an empty set, matching npm. The docstring's "any version" is read as "any release version."
- **Whole spec is validated:** a malformed set raises even when an earlier set already matched, e.g. `1.0.0 || garbage` raises for `1.0.0`.
- **Operators must attach to the version:** `>= 1.2.3` is rejected as malformed, since whitespace is only ignored around `||` and between comparators.
- **Strict tokens:** `X` (uppercase) wildcards, build metadata (`+build`), and non-ASCII digits are rejected. Digits are `[0-9]`, not Python's `\d`, which would accept other Unicode digits.

The project isn't a git repository, so there's no diff and I didn't commit anything.
